title: Use more skips to prevent attack-card dilution
situation: When the deck already contains several strong attacks or duplicate cards and a reward offers another narrow damage card.
lesson: Skip marginal attack rewards more often and prioritize cards that improve consistency, defense, or scaling. Avoid adding duplicates merely because they are immediately playable; a smaller deck makes key defensive and setup cards appear more reliably.
evidence_points: The final deck contained 33 cards, including five Bites, two Angers, two Carnages, two Uppercuts, and two Flame Barriers.
Early rewards repeatedly added damage cards: Carnage, Cleave, Anger, Wild Strike, a second Carnage, and later additional attack cards.
At Act 2 Floor 28, three identical reward screens were skipped, but Clothesline+ was eventually taken from the same low-impact pool.
reasoning: The final build had substantial attack redundancy and many repeated cards, while the boss combat still reached turns with hands dominated by Angers and limited immediate defense. More disciplined skipping earlier would have reduced dilution and improved access to the deck's stronger defensive and scaling tools.

title: At critical HP, draw before committing to expensive setup
situation: In a boss fight at very low HP, when the enemy is not currently attacking and draw or hand-manipulation cards are legal.
lesson: Consider using available draw tools before playing a costly long-term power if doing so can find block or recovery. Do not automatically spend the entire turn on Demon Form when the player is near lethal and has Battle Trance or Burning Pact available.
evidence_points: On Turn 11, at 15/85 HP with 3 energy and 6 block, Demon Form, Battle Trance, and Burning Pact were all legal alternatives while the Automaton's intent was DEFEND_BUFF.
Demon Form was chosen, leaving 0 energy; the following hand still contained Battle Trance, Burning Pact, Second Wind, Bite, and Power Through.
On Turn 12, the player had 0 block while the Automaton's intent was ATTACK and then spent the turn on Bite and multiple Angers rather than having established a defensive hand.
reasoning: The non-attacking enemy intent provided a window to improve the next hand. Choosing Demon Form immediately consumed all energy without producing block, and the subsequent attack turn began with no block. The exact optimal line cannot be proven from the compact log, but prioritizing draw and stabilization here is a strong reusable hypothesis.

title: Treat Gremlin Nob skills as a major cost
situation: When fighting Gremlin Nob, especially after HP has fallen below half and Nob is attacking, reassess every skill before playing it.
lesson: Minimize nonessential skills against Nob and prioritize a direct attack or a clearly necessary block. Avoid spending a turn on multiple setup skills that leave the strongest attacks unplayable, since Nob punishes skill-heavy turns.
evidence_points: On turn 4 at 19/80 HP, the agent played Battle Trance, then Thunderclap, then Armaments, and finally used its last energy on Defend while Gremlin Nob remained at 30 HP.
Earlier, on turn 3 at 23/80 HP, the agent played Searing Blow+1 and Strike without gaining block, and Nob continued attacking while only partially damaged.
The fight ended at 19/80 HP with Gremlin Nob still at 30/86 HP.
reasoning: The logged sequence shows repeated setup and skill use during a lethal-pressure fight, while the resulting energy state prevented the available high-damage cards from being used. Against Nob, this pattern both increases his strength through skills and delays ending the fight.

title: Do not keep adding damage cards when the deck lacks resilience
situation: After the early rewards have already supplied several attacks and setup cards, particularly when HP is falling through Act 1.
lesson: Prefer skipping speculative damage/build-around cards when no clearly efficient defensive option is offered, rather than continuing to add attacks that do not solve incoming damage. Build enough reliable defense or mitigation to preserve HP for elites and the boss.
evidence_points: The final 17-card deck contained five Strikes, four Defends, Searing Blow+1, Perfected Strike, Thunderclap, Clothesline, Headbutt, Armaments, and Battle Trance; the only permanent basic block cards were the four Defends plus Armaments.
The run's HP fell from 71/80 after floor 5 to 32/80 after floor 7, then reached 27/80 after floor 8.
The later reward choices added Perfected Strike and Thunderclap after Searing Blow had already been taken and upgraded.
reasoning: The final list confirms a damage- and setup-heavy deck without a substantial new defensive package, while the HP trajectory shows that this imbalance mattered before the elite. Since skipping was available at the later rewards, declining marginal attack cards would have been a safer default when they did not address survivability.
